episode_summary: Episode 308 (May 2020): the hosts discuss the upcoming Bitcoin halving and price, explain public-key cryptography and digital signatures, then interview Fazri Zubair, CTO of LucidSight, about the blockchain games Crypto Space Commander and MLB Champions and their in-game economies.

cards.claim: In May 2020 Bitcoin had repeatedly touched and dropped back from $10,000 before the halving.
cards.speaker: host
cards.quote: It's seen 10,000 and dropped. It's been above 10,000 and dropped. It hit 10,000 again.

cards.claim: In May 2020 a host relayed Willy Woo's view that large exchanges, not miners, would increasingly set the Bitcoin price.
cards.speaker: host
cards.quote: he thinks that large exchanges are now going to determine the price because they hold most of it.

cards.claim: In May 2020, ahead of the third Bitcoin halving, hosts explained that miner block rewards would be cut in half.
cards.speaker: host
cards.quote: it's going to be cut in half and that means that basically the amount of money that miners are making is cut in half

cards.claim: In May 2020 a host explained that Bitcoin's block subsidy halves roughly every four years on a geometrically decreasing curve.
cards.speaker: host
cards.quote: This is on a geometrically decreasing curve over time that halves every four years.

cards.claim: In May 2020 a host predicted Bitcoin's network security would decline after the halving unless transaction fees rose enough to replace lost block rewards.
cards.speaker: host
cards.quote: the inevitable conclusion is that the quote unquote security of the Bitcoin network will go down

cards.claim: In May 2020 hosts observed that Ether's price was starting to decouple from Bitcoin.
cards.speaker: host
cards.quote: Ether is starting to decouple from Bitcoin as far as its behavior.

cards.claim: In May 2020 a host explained public-key encryption: anyone can encrypt to your public key, but only your private key can decrypt the message.
cards.speaker: host
cards.quote: the only person that's capable of decrypting that thing is going to be me with my private key.

cards.claim: In May 2020 a host explained that each blockchain transaction is digitally signed with the sender's private key so miners can verify it came from that address.
cards.speaker: host
cards.quote: when i make a transaction i'm signing it with my private key so that everyone knows it came from a specific public key

cards.claim: In May 2020 a host argued that digital uniqueness and ownership had become permanent, so people must take responsibility for their digital identity.
cards.speaker: host
cards.quote: digital uniqueness is a thing that's out of the box now and it's not coming back

cards.claim: In May 2020 Fazri Zubair said LucidSight was founded in 2015 as a game development studio in Santa Monica.
cards.speaker: Fazri Zubair
cards.quote: LucidSight was founded in 2015 as a game development studio here in Santa Monica.

cards.claim: In May 2020 LucidSight said its MLB Champions was a licensed Major League Baseball game made with MLB and the MLB Players Association.
cards.speaker: Fazri Zubair
cards.quote: it's a licensed major league baseball game with both the mlb and the mlb pa

cards.claim: In May 2020 Fazri Zubair said Crypto Space Commander had been in early access for about six months.
cards.speaker: Fazri Zubair
cards.quote: This is a social economic driven game that's been live now in early access for about six months

cards.claim: Fazri Zubair recounted an EVE Online incident in which a large in-game bank took its members' money and bought the biggest ship possible.
cards.speaker: Fazri Zubair
cards.quote: basically just said, screw y'all, I'm taking all your money, bought the biggest ship that was possible

cards.claim: In May 2020 LucidSight said a dreadnought ship in its game had sold for $42,000.
cards.speaker: Fazri Zubair
cards.quote: We have a dreadnought in our game that's sold for $42,000.

cards.claim: In May 2020 LucidSight said its Enterprise ship had sold for $30,000.
cards.speaker: Fazri Zubair
cards.quote: our enterprise sold for 30 000

cards.claim: In May 2020 Fazri Zubair said that after full persistence launched, a destroyed ship's blockchain record would be burned.
cards.speaker: Fazri Zubair
cards.quote: ship gets destroyed we burn the blockchain record it's gone that asset is nullified

cards.claim: In May 2020 LucidSight said Crypto Space Commander was doing about $100,000 of player-to-player volume a day.
cards.speaker: Fazri Zubair
cards.quote: But we do $100,000 of volume a day in CSE right now.

cards.claim: Fazri Zubair described Trilite as a scarce resource in Crypto Space Commander that is used to craft almost everything and found only in the fringe space.
cards.speaker: Fazri Zubair
cards.quote: We have a resource, one of our largest commodities in the game called Trilite. It's used for crafting almost everything.

cards.claim: Fazri Zubair said LucidSight built Scarcity Engine, an off-chain system that emulates Ethereum on fast databases, so about 99% of game actions happen off-chain.
cards.speaker: Fazri Zubair
cards.quote: We created our own system called Scarcity Engine, which emulates Ethereum blockchain but on high-speed databases with high-speed APIs.

cards.claim: Fazri Zubair described GALE, LucidSight's analytics system that assigns dollar values to in-game resources and items.
cards.speaker: Fazri Zubair
cards.quote: We have this system that we kind of built. It's an analytics system called a GALE.

cards.claim: Fazri Zubair said one ton of iron mined in Crypto Space Commander could be used to craft about 1,400 different items.
cards.speaker: Fazri Zubair
cards.quote: if you mine one ton of iron, that one ton of iron could be used to create about 1400 different items.

cards.claim: In April 2020 LucidSight sold station facilities in Crypto Space Commander, and more than 50 sold out within the first day.
cards.speaker: Fazri Zubair
cards.quote: within the first day over 50 were sold out and most of them were bought by you know large groups of players

cards.claim: In May 2020 LucidSight said item destruction on ship loss would begin within about two weeks, burning around half of a destroyed ship's equipment.
cards.speaker: Fazri Zubair
cards.quote: After about, in the next two weeks here, destruction will happen.

cards.claim: Fazri Zubair said that when Gale first launched, a mined resource in Crypto Space Commander showed a value of $1 million, which was corrected as data accumulated.
cards.speaker: Fazri Zubair
cards.quote: When you mined one of it, it said it was worth a million dollars.

cards.claim: A host said Diablo 3's real-money auction house capped sales at about $500 per item, and players bought the game to flip loot for profit.
cards.speaker: host
cards.quote: I think the maximum you could make was $500 for any given item.

cards.claim: A host said the majority of the Diablo 3 real-money auction house user base was botted accounts.
cards.speaker: host
cards.quote: the majority of the user base was botted accounts

cards.claim: In May 2020 Fazri Zubair said MLB Champions had recently launched on iOS and Android and was at about 40,000 monthly active users.
cards.speaker: Fazri Zubair
cards.quote: MLB Champions recently launched on iOS and Android. We're up to like 40,000 monthly active users.

cards.claim: Fazri Zubair said MLB Champions NFTs could never be destroyed because its contract had no burn function, unlike Crypto Space Commander.
cards.speaker: Fazri Zubair
cards.quote: once you mint a figure, it can never be destroyed. By the design of the contract, we have no burn functionality in it, unlike CSC.

cards.claim: Fazri Zubair argued players should be able to sell digital items such as Fortnite skins and recoup their value when they move to another game.
cards.speaker: Fazri Zubair
cards.quote: And if you play Fortnite and you buy 100 skins and you decide you're done with Fortnite

cards.claim: Fazri Zubair said an iridium spike when players found a node doubled the total iridium in Crypto Space Commander, and the economic indicators flagged it within 24 hours.
cards.speaker: Fazri Zubair
cards.quote: It actually doubled the entire amount that existed in the universe at that time.

cards.claim: Fazri Zubair said Crypto Space Commander's 24 core resources are technically ERC-20 tokens that can be checked out and burned to create virtual items.
cards.speaker: Fazri Zubair
cards.quote: Those are technically ERC-20. So when you check them out of the system, you could actually get a token for them.

cards.claim: In May 2020 a host said many blockchain-game companies interviewed in 2017 were really using Amazon web servers while claiming to use the blockchain.
cards.speaker: host
cards.quote: they were just using a bunch of Amazon web servers and lying about it.

title: The Bitcoin Podcast #308- Fazri Zubair Lucid Sights
